note: Ratchet baseline for the host-assumption guard.  These entries are PRE-EXISTING: absolute-path literals in tests that are deliberate inputs (a path that must be rejected) and capability uses that already skip.  The gate fails on anything NEW, so a new absolute path or an un-skipped capability use must be fixed rather than silently added.  The identity is rule|relative_path|FULL_VALUE, so entries are exact.

rationales.host-absolute-path|tests/support/p5_proc: Linux kernel procfs PID state, checked only after the Windows branch returns and only when the stat file exists. It distinguishes already terminated zombies from running leaked children; this is an OS interface, not a fixture tied to one host directory. No concatenation workaround or global exemption.
rationales.host-absolute-path|tests/test_local_prep: Deliberately malicious schema_version input; compared only as opaque JSON/string data and never passed to Path, filesystem, subprocess cwd or a host capability. The same rejection must hold on every operating system. This exact fixture closes the independent-review physical-address leak; it is not a host-specific expected path or a blanket test exemption.
